title: Elmwood Health – integration brain dump
content:
Context / quick summary:
- Elmwood Health (regional hospital chain, 6 hospitals + telehealth) exploring an on-prem / VPC Private deployment for triage assistant + discharge-summary generation. Primary drivers: PHI residency, auditability, and deterministic latency for clinician workflows.
- Initial ask: prototype that ingests EHR progress notes (HL7/FHIR), extracts problem list + medication changes, and drafts a one-paragraph discharge summary suitable for clinician edit.
- Risk/constraints called out repeatedly by Elmwood: strict PHI handling, hospital infosec requires no tokens leave VPC, Syslog-compatible audit trails, and KMS/HSM for key management.

Who was on the call:
- Elmwood: Dr. Karen Liu (CMIO), Marcus D'Souza (SRE), Priya Rao (Clinical informatics)
- Redwood: Sofia Patel (SE), Diego Ramos (solutions eng), Nina Park (security partner)

Notes from convo / highlights:
- Data flow they want: EHR -> middleware (internal) -> Redwood Private inference (inside their VPC) -> result returns to middleware -> EHR UI. Emphasized minimal hops and synchronous < 1.2s median to preserve clinician flow for short notes.
- They have a batch use-case too (overnight summaries) where throughput matters more than latency; willing to accept lower-cost quantized models for batch.
- PHI classification: everything in progress notes flagged PHI. They require redact+audit if anything leaves customer boundaries. This rules out hosted API. Private only.
- Auditing: retention 365 days, immutable append-only logs exported to their SIEM. Must support per-request metadata (user id, patient MRN hashed, route).
- Model explainability: clinicians want a traceable token-to-output mapping for some high-risk fields (diagnoses change). Not expecting full token-level provenance but want attribution-ish notes (which prompt lines influenced summary).
- Regulatory: possible state-level constraints around mental health notes; need redaction options and a policy to exclude certain note types from automatic summarization.

Technical constraints / architecture considerations:
- Preferred infra: Elmwood runs on AWS GovCloud-like isolation in a VPC; they are open to a Redwood Private control plane with customer-managed networking.
- Hardware: their infra team prefers 2x A100-class or equivalent for early prototype (they already have a small GPU pool). For production would want Dedicated-like reserved capacity but on-prem.
- Model choices: customer leans toward a smaller fine-tuned open-source model (instruction-tuned, medically-aligned) to keep costs down and reduce hallucination risk. We suggested comparing 7B/13B quantized variants + our curated med model if available.
- Tokenization/costs: large notes (progress notes ~2k tokens) — need prefix/KV caching per patient visit to avoid re-encoding shared context for multi-step edits. Suggest session affinity routing.
- Streaming: for the UI edit flow, streaming partial summary tokens could improve perceived latency; we need to validate integration with their middleware that expects chunked HTTP/WS.
- Security: KMS integration required (customer-managed keys, HSM preferred). Need to support FIPS endpoints.
- Networking: allowlist IPs and mutual TLS between their middleware and Redwood runtime endpoints inside the VPC.

Gotchas called out / potential pitfalls:
- Data residency vs. control plane: they will accept a Redwood control plane outside their VPC only if metadata and model artifacts are non-PII and they can sign an agreement — strongly prefer fully private control plane.
- EHR attachments and images: Elmwood wants future OCR for scanned docs; we must call that out as out-of-scope for MVP. If they push, estimate +4–6 weeks and need GPU memory planning.
- Persistence of KV cache: if we use per-visit cache, eviction policies must be explicit (e.g., evict after discharge). Otherwise cache could leak PHI across patients in mistakes.
- Fine-tuning vs. prompt engineering: their compliance team will prefer prompt engineering + guardrails (redaction, classifier pre-check) over storing new weights unless we provide an auditable fine-tuning pipeline.
- Logging volume: audit logs per request + token counts will be large; recommend separate pipeline to S3 -> SIEM; budget for log egress within their infra.

Open questions (need answers from Elmwood):
- Q1: Which EHR vendor + version? (Dr. Liu said 'Cerner-ish cluster' — get exact). Ticket created: JIRA EH-1023 to confirm.
- Q2: Exact latency SLO— they said 1.2s median for interactive flow; confirm 95th percentile SLO allowed.
- Q3: Are their clinicians ok with partial streaming or do they require final complete text before presenting? UI UX decision.
- Q4: Does their legal team require the control plane to be in-customer account (yes/no)?
- Q5: Is there an internal patient-consent policy affecting automated summarization of psych/behavioral notes?

Immediate next steps / owners (week-of actions):
- Sofia: create two prototype architecture sketches — (A) fully private control plane + runtime in customer VPC, (B) customer-runtime + Redwood-managed control plane with metadata-only tokens. Due: 2026-03-15. Linked: confluence:EH-integration-playbook.
- Diego: run cost/latency sim (approx lookups) for 7B vs 13B quantized models with prefix caching on 2xA100. Deliver rough estimate and ops-risk notes. Due: 2026-03-18.
- Nina: security checklist draft for Elmwood (KMS, FIPS, mutual TLS, SIEM export schema). Pull from private-deploy security template. Due: 2026-03-12.
- Marcus (Elmwood SRE): share EHR export sample (de-identified first) and network architecture diagram. Asked to post to Slack #eh-pilot by 2026-03-13.
- Create a short demo plan (30m) focusing on: single-note summarization (interactive), batch overnight run, and audit log review. Tentative demo week: 2026-03-22.

Prototype acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Summaries produced inside Elmwood VPC, no tokens leave customer boundaries.
- Median latency for interactive summarization <= 1.2s on provided sample notes (measured on their infra).
- Audit logs emitted per request to customer's SIEM, retained 365d.
- Redaction step present: any note type flagged as "sensitive" excluded from auto-summarize and routed to manual queue.
- Clinician editing flow: ability to accept/modify generated summary and write-back partial metadata to EHR.

Notes to myself / rough brainstorm:
- Could use lightweight classifier (small embed model) on-prem to gate notes before sending to generator (cheap way to exclude PHI categories). Put classifier inline as pre-check to avoid expensive calls.
- Explore using local quantized med model + Redwood runtime for streaming — need to test memory footprint with multi-session caching.
- Consider canary policy: for first 2 weeks, write generated summaries to "draft" field only, not live discharge note. Ramp to 50%/100% after manual audits.

Slack snippets / PR references to drop into follow ups:
- "@Marcus send EHR sample + network diagram — we need: hostname, CIDR, firewall pairings, and any packet inspection boxes."
- PR note: link to EH-1023, confluence:EH-integration-playbook, sec-template:private-deploy

Decision log (to date):
- Decided: Private deployment required, no hosted API.
- Decided: MVP will not include image OCR or multimodal inputs.

Misc smaller items:
- Add Elmwood to internal pilot tracker sheet (sheet:pilot-tracker-2026).
- Prep a short clinician-facing one-pager explaining how model suggestions are produced and how to revert. Useful for adoption and legal.

End of notes.

(rough, shareable — can clean into a one-pager after Nina's security checklist is in).
